benefits: Search engines discover every page: sitemaps help crawlers find pages that few sites link to.
No manual XML writing: paste a list of URLs and get a valid sitemap.xml in one click.

Upload-ready file: the download is a standards-compliant sitemap.xml for Google Search Console.

faqs.a: A sitemap.xml is a file listing all the pages of a website that you want search engines to crawl. Search engines read it to discover pages, learn update frequencies and prioritize crawling.

After generating it, upload sitemap.xml to the root of your website (e.g. https://example.com/sitemap.xml) and submit that URL in Google Search Console under Sitemaps. Also reference it in robots.txt.
faqs.q: Where do I put the generated sitemap?

faqs.a: The tool checks every line: it must be a valid http:// or https:// URL. Lines that fail are counted as invalid and skipped, and exact duplicates (ignoring URL fragments) are removed. A summary shows valid, invalid and duplicate counts.
faqs.q: What happens to invalid or duplicate URLs?

faqs.a: The sitemap protocol caps one file at 50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed. If your site is larger, split the list and create a sitemap index file linking the parts.
faqs.q: Is there a limit to how many URLs I can include?

faqs.a: changefreq is only a hint to crawlers, not a promise. Use values that reflect reality: daily for news, weekly for blogs, monthly or yearly for mostly static pages. lastmod should be the real last modification date of each page.
faqs.q: What changefreq and lastmod should I use?

faqs.a: Yes, all of it runs in your browser. Your URL list is never uploaded anywhere, so private or unreleased pages stay private.

xml-sitemap-generator.formula:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/page</loc>
    <lastmod>2026-10-18</lastmod>
    <changefreq>weekly</changefreq>
    <priority>0.5</priority>
  </url>
</urlset>
One <url> block per page. <loc> is required; the other three are optional.
howTo: Paste your page URLs into the box, one URL per line.
Choose a changefreq hint (how often the pages change).
Set a priority between 0.0 and 1.0 (1.0 = most important).
Keep lastmod on to stamp each entry with today's date.
Copy the XML or download it as sitemap.xml, then upload it to your site root.
keyFacts: sitemap.xml follows the Sitemaps protocol (sitemaps.org), supported by Google, Bing and other search engines since 2006.
A sitemap does not guarantee indexing, but it helps crawlers discover and prioritize your pages.
Each <url> entry must contain an absolute <loc>; <lastmod>, <changefreq> and <priority> are optional hints.
One sitemap file holds at most 50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed.
Special characters in URLs are escaped automatically (e.g. & becomes &) so the XML stays valid.
URL fragments (#section) are stripped, because search engines index the page, not the fragment.

limitations: A sitemap helps discovery but never guarantees that Google will index a page.
changefreq and priority are hints only; crawlers may ignore them.
Very large sites need multiple sitemap files plus a sitemap index; this tool makes one file at a time.
The lastmod stamp uses today's date for every entry; per-page real dates need a crawler-based generator.
